params.body:
## Why

Between 16 and 21 September 2026, 30 portal vehicles were removed here while their `delete` never left: `VehiclePublisher::removed` spoke to Nederland Mobiel before ringing, and a request killed there never reached the bell (finding `een-webhook-zonder-sessie`, fixed in #840). That fix works forward only. The open point `2026-09-28-de-dertig-wagens-staan-mogelijk-nog-bij-een-portaal` still stands: those vehicles may still be listed at the receivers.

## What

`php artisan stocklist:resend-removals [--since=2026-09-15] [--vehicle=<id> ...] [--apply]`

The selection comes from the data, not from a list of ids. Per vehicle and per receiver:

- the vehicle is soft-deleted on or after the floor, complete (an incomplete vehicle never rings, R S2-10.5), and was published: a row in `vehicle_portals` or `send_to_modix` still on;
- the receiver is one the ring reaches (the dealer's plus the platform-wide ones, R S2-10.7), still exists, and existed when the vehicle was removed;
- the last successful delivery to that receiver about that vehicle is not a `delete` or `sold`. A failed delivery does not count, and a `create` after a `delete` means the receiver's last word is that the car is there.

The floor is the later of `--since` and the oldest row in `webhook_deliveries`. That table only writes from 15 September 2026 and is pruned after 30 days, and before its first row a missing delivery proves nothing. The command prints that limit.

Without `--apply` it only lists: id, dealer, make and model, deleted_at, a marker when the vehicle is still flagged on Nederland Mobiel, and the receivers that would get the `delete`. With `--apply` it goes through `WebhookHelper::dispatchVehicleWebhookJobs('delete', $vehicle, true, $receiverIds)`, so the seal, the dealer, the queue (`webhook`) and the payload are exactly those of the observer's path; the only addition is an optional list of receiver ids so a receiver that already got the removal is not called again. With the seal closed it queues nothing, says why and exits 1.

Idempotent: every arrival is recorded in `webhook_deliveries`, so a second run after the queue has drained lists nothing. What is still listed then did not arrive.

Nederland Mobiel is not touched. The removal path does talk to it (with a 30 second timeout since 20 September 2026), but whether those adverts are still up is a question for that partner, and this command is about the webhook receivers.

## Rules

- New rule R S2-10.14 in `12-s2-eigen-wagenpark-publiceren.md`.
- The open point on the thirty vehicles now names the command; the decision to run `--apply` stays open there. It also no longer claims the ids are listed in the finding (they were not).

## Tests

`tests/Feature/ResendRemovalsCommandTest.php` (`@rule S2-10.14`, one `@rule S2-10.10`): dry run lists and sends nothing; `--apply` queues a `delete` only to receivers that missed it (partial delivery, republished after a delete, failed delete, other dealer's receiver untouched); only published, complete vehicles after the floor are listed; a second run after delivery sends nothing; a closed seal queues nothing. Full suite green locally.
params.title: Resend the removals the webhook receivers never got
